LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAA:
The game crashed because the mod files were extracted.
Simply place the mod files into the folder without extracting them; otherwise, the game will crash.

Launch the game once you have dealt with the mod files.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAB:
The game crashed because Minecraft has exhausted its allocated memory.
This is likely due to insufficient system memory, inadequate memory allocation, or excessively high performance requirements.

Consider running "Memory optimization" under "More → Utilities," then relaunch the game.
If the issue persists, consider increasing the memory allocated to the game in the launch settings, or remove textures, mods, and shaders with high performance requirements.
If the problem continues, consider closing other applications before launching the game, or... perhaps using a different computer?
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAC:
The game crashed due to the use of OpenJ9.
Switch to a non-OpenJ9 Java version in "Settings → Game → Java" and relaunch the game.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAD:
The game appears to have crashed due to the use of JDK or an excessively high Java version.
Switch to JRE 8 (Java 8) in "Settings → Launch → Java" and relaunch the game.
Download and install one on the internet if you do not have JRE 8 installed.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAE:
The game appears to have crashed due to the use of excessively high Java version.
Consider selecting a lower Java version in "Settings → Launch → Java" and relaunch the game.
Download and install one on the internet if you do not have any installed.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAF:
The game is incompatible with the Java version you are currently using.
Download and install one on the internet if you do not have any suitable installed.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAG:
The game crashed because the mod names contains special characters.
Consider modifying the file names to include only letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores, and periods, then relaunch the game.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAH:
The game crashed because the MixinBootstrap is missing.
Consider installing MixinBootstrap. If the issue persists, try to add an exclamation mark at the beginning of the file name.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAI:
The game crashed due to the use of a 32-bit Java, which can prevent Minecraft from accessing the necessary memory.

Consider selecting a 64-bit Java in "Settings → Launch → Java" and relaunch the game.
Download and install one on the internet if you do not have 64-bit Java installed.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAJ:
The game crashed due to the use of a 32-bit operating system, which can prevent Minecraft from accessing the necessary memory.

You may only resolve this issue by installing a 64-bit operating system.
If your computer has less than 2GB of memory, you may need to consider using a different computer with more memory...

 - If it persists, the issue may originate from other factors...
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonAZ:

Consider creating a new world and monitor the performance of the game:
 - If it operates normally, it is likely that some blocks were the source of the error, and you may need to delete this world.
 - If it persists, the issue may originate from other factors...
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonBB:
The game crashed due to the duplicate mods.

Each mod must be unique. Make sure to remove any duplicate mods before relaunching the game.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonBE:
The game crashed due to the incompatibility between OptiFine and the current version of Forge.

Consider visiting the OptiFine website (https://optifine.net/downloads) and reinstalling the game using the corresponding compatible version strictly.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonBF:
Shader mods are unnecessary since OptiFine has incorporated their features.
Removing the shader mods allows the game to run normally.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonBG:
The game crashed due to the incompatibility between the outdated version of Forge and the current Java.

Consider the following solutions:
 - Update Forge to version 36.2.26 or higher.
 - Use a Java version lower than 1.8.0_320.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonBH:
The game crashed potentially because the Forge version was modified by other launchers, resulting in abnormal files within the instance.

The game crashed because the graphics driver has issues, or a dedicated graphics card was not in use.

If you have a dedicated graphics card, use it instead of the Intel integrated graphics card when launching PCL and Minecraft.
If the issue persists, consider updating your graphics card driver to the latest version, or rolling back to the factory version.
If the problem continues, consider using Java version 8.0.51 or lower.
LangModCrashCrashReasonReasonBN:
The game crashed due to graphics driver issues.

Consider updating your graphics card driver to the latest version, or rolling back to the factory version, and relaunch the game.

LangPageSetupLaunchLaunchAdvanceOptionsC:
Executes the specific command or program before launching Minecraft. The syntax is same as the batch script.

Relative paths can be implemented with the following alternate tags (paths end with "\"):
 · {path}: The folder where the PCL is located
 · {minecraft}: .minecraft folder
 · {verpath}: Instance folder (.minecraft\versions\<instance name>\)
 · {verindie}: The instance folder when instance isolation is enabled, or the .minecraft folder when disabled
 · {java}: The folder of the Java used by the game

Additionally, the following alternate tags are also supported:
 · {user}: Username
 · {login}: Login method
 · {uuid}: Player's UUID
 · {name}: Instance name
 · {date}, {time}: System time
 · {version}: Vanilla game version

For example:
 · [ {verpath}test.exe ] : Run the test.exe program in the instance folder.
 · [ "{java}java.exe" -jar "{verpath}test.jar" ] : Run the test.jar file in the instance folder using Java.
 · [ notepad "{verindie}option.txt" ] : Use Notepad to open option.txt of this instance.

It is best to put quotation marks (") around operations involving paths to avoid failures due to spaces in the path.
When executing a command, the directory where the Command Prompt is located is the current .minecraft folder.

LangPageVersionSetupCommand:
This option will not override the global settings: The command for the global settings will be executed before the one for the instance.

Executes the specific command or program before launching Minecraft. The syntax is same as the batch script.

Relative paths can be implemented with the following alternate tags (paths end with "\"):
 · {path}: The folder where the PCL is located
 · {minecraft}: .minecraft folder
 · {verpath}: Instance folder (.minecraft\versions\<instance name>\)
 · {verindie}: The instance folder when instance isolation is enabled, or the .minecraft folder when disabled
 · {java}: The folder of the Java used by the game

Additionally, the following alternate tags are also supported:
 · {user}: Username
 · {login}: Login method
 · {uuid}: Player's UUID
 · {name}: Instance name
 · {date}, {time}: System time
 · {version}: Vanilla game version

For example:
 · [ {verpath}test.exe ] : Run the test.exe program in the instance folder.
 · [ "{java}java.exe" -jar "{verpath}test.jar" ] : Run the test.jar file in the instance folder using Java.
 · [ notepad "{verindie}option.txt" ] : Use Notepad to open option.txt of this instance.

It is best to put quotation marks (") around operations involving paths to avoid failures due to spaces in the path.
When executing a command, the directory where the Command Prompt is located is the current .minecraft folder.
